## [0.0.4] - 2026-11-15

### Changed

- Admits OpenCode 2.3: the supported range is `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0` (`opencode.host` in `package.json`).
  The plugin is tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7 and 2.3.0: `TESTED_HOSTS` in `src/hosts.ts` is that list,
  and the host and pack tests install every release in it, so CI now runs stock OpenCode 2.2.7 and 2.3.0 too. The out-of-range example in the docs
  and tests is now 2.4.0.
- The host test waits until `granola.meetings` has activated in every test project, and until the `plan` agent is
  listed, before any case runs: stock 2.2.7 and 2.3.0 answer a location's first requests before its plugins have
  loaded, where 2.2.6 waited.
- What OpenCode 2.3 changes does not reach this plugin: it runs no subagents and does not subscribe to
  `session.tool.failed` (it listens only for `integration.updated` and `mcp.status.changed`), and it has no use for the
  new `session.fork` hook. The long-running tools, the Markdown export and `events_list`, already stop when the
  person presses Stop and the tool's signal aborts.
- The icon is now Granola's own mark, Granola's swirl on Granola's lime, as in Granola's own app icon, in place of the family's drawn mark; `opencode.vendor.mark` is `true`, and the README says Granola is a trademark of Granola, Inc.

### Known limits

- **Granola's server decides what the tools reach.** The plugin registers the tools Granola's server lists. A tool Granola adds later is not classed by the plugin: the `access` option decides whether it runs, asks or is denied, and `/granola-status` counts it as unknown.
- **Plan limits.** Granola's free plan has no transcripts or folders, and its meeting history covers the last 30 days. Exports say what is missing rather than working around it.
- **Exports are bounded.** An export takes 1 to 20 meetings and at most 8 MB; a transcript that does not fit is cut with a note. The file goes outside the project, so OpenCode also asks for `external_directory`.
- **`give_feedback` reaches Granola's team.** It is allowed by default, and the skill tells the model to send it only when the user asks.
- **No retries.** The plugin does not retry a failed call. The error names the next step.
- **The meetings source sees what Granola's MCP sees.** Granola's MCP reads only the active workspace, and on the free (Basic) plan only notes from the last 30 days; its rate limits vary by plan and tool and average about 100 requests per minute across all tools ([Granola MCP](https://docs.granola.ai/help-center/sharing/integrations/mcp)). A listing reads `search_meetings` once per page of each week, and `get_meetings` once per 10 meetings. A cursor never expires, and a listing cannot tell when the plan hides older meetings, so it never reports a gap: a cursor older than 30 days on the free plan lists only what the plan still shows. Switching the active workspace changes what a listing reads under the same account.
- **The meetings source's test data is invented.** The conformance kit runs on a synthetic Granola whose answers follow the shapes Granola's live tools returned when last checked, and the note-access scopes as `get_account_info`'s own description gives them; their content is made up, modelled on the provider's docs, not live-verified. Its report is incomplete on one check, the expired cursor, because the source never answers `CURSOR_EXPIRED`.
- **Hosts and platforms.** The plugin is tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7 and 2.3.0, and runs on macOS or Linux. A later 2.2 or 2.3 release starts and is reported as untested.
- In Jelly, the `access` setting is drawn as a choice of three, which needs a Jelly that reads declared choices: an
  older Jelly refuses the plugin's whole declaration.
- Updates are not automatic for a Git install, and `opencode plugin update` and `opencode plugin check` do not work on one: to move to a newer release, remove the old entry and add the new tag.

## [0.0.3] - 2026-11-15

### Added

- Granola's meetings as a source under the shared source contract, `@we-the-rebel-alliance/source-contract` v0.1.0:
  `package.json`'s new top-level `sources` key declares `granola.meetings`, an `events` source of kind `meeting` read
  with `events_list` (input `source` `granola`), with named accounts (`accounts.named: true`: every read names the
  signed-in email, which `probe` answers), private, `cost.class: "free"`, `maxBytes` 65,536, with exactly the
  Granola tools its reads call as its operations (`get_account_info`, `search_meetings`, `get_meetings`),
  `get_account_info` as its one identity operation, the tools RPC `granola.meetings.tools` and the probe action
  `granola_probe`. Memory and jelly read the declaration from the installed package, with the contract's `descriptor`.
- For Memory and jelly: the tools RPC method `probe` (action `granola_probe`, allowed by the default rules at every
  `access`) answers who is signed in, `{ source, account, owner, scopes, trust }`, from one `get_account_info` read:
  the account is the signed-in email, the owner `mailto:` and that email (labelled with the email, as on every page),
  and `scopes` Granola's note-access scopes (`personal`, `public`). It refuses another account with
  `ACCOUNT_MISMATCH`.
- A page also carries `plugin`, `asOf` and `refused[]`: a meeting whose title or summary holds a secret is refused for
  good with `reason: "secret"`, and the cursor moves past it.
- The conformance kit runs over the declared source in `npm run check` (in `npm test`, `test/conformance.test.ts`), on
  the synthetic Granola with no Granola call, and writes `reports/conformance-report.json` (git-ignored, the same bytes
  every run) for a release to attach. Every check that applies passes. The report stays incomplete on the kit's
  expired-cursor check: a cursor is a meeting's start and ID, which never expire, and a listing cannot tell when the
  free plan's 30-day window hides older meetings, so it never answers `CURSOR_EXPIRED` (the README's Known limits).

### Changed

- For Memory and every consumer, required input: every `events_list` call names `account`, the signed-in Granola
  email that `probe` answers (any case; pages name it lowercase). A listing without it is refused with
  `INPUT_INVALID`, and so is `default`, which a consumer fills for an unnamed source. `events_list` never reads
  `get_account_info` any more: the page's account and owner are the account it names, and every `get_meetings`
  answer must name that account, as a `<connected_user_email>` element or a `connected_user_email` attribute of
  `<meetings_data>`. Another account is `ACCOUNT_MISMATCH`; an answer that holds meetings and names none is
  `UNAVAILABLE`, and a page lists nothing unless at least one answer named the account, so the check never passes for
  want of an answer.
- For Memory, a cursor restart: the account every page and event names is now the signed-in email instead of
  `default`, and the cursor is the contract's bound cursor (plugin `granola`, source `granola`, the account). A cursor
  an earlier version issued is refused with `CURSOR_INVALID`; start again with `since`. A cursor passed with another
  account is refused with `ACCOUNT_MISMATCH` before any read. The owner is unchanged: `mailto:` and the email,
  labelled with the email.
- The error codes of `events_list` are the source contract's: `INPUT_INVALID`, `CURSOR_INVALID`, `ACCOUNT_MISMATCH`,
  `SOURCE_UNKNOWN` and `UNAVAILABLE` (Granola's own failure) replace `EVENTS_INVALID_INPUT`, `EVENTS_CURSOR_INVALID`,
  `EVENTS_ACCOUNT_UNKNOWN`, `EVENTS_SOURCE_UNKNOWN`, `EVENTS_OWNER_UNKNOWN` and `EVENTS_READ_FAILED`.
- A page holds at most 64 KiB of JSON (the contract's default and the host's RPC cap), instead of 900,000 bytes, so a
  run of long summaries takes more pages.
- The tools RPC and the events contract are the source contract's, bundled into `dist/index.js` from the pinned tag;
  `src/host/tools-rpc

## [0.0.2] - 2026-11-14

### Added

- Jelly's declaration lists the three tools Granola serves that it lacked: `get_agent_brief` (a read),
  `create_meeting_note_from_transcript` (a write) and `sign_out` (a change, still hidden from agents, with a note on how
  to sign out). A read-only helper in Jelly is never given the last two. The plugin knows the first two as a read and a
  write, so they follow `access` and are tools RPC methods.
- `test/fixtures/live-tools.json`, Granola's tool list captured live on 14 November 2026, and a test that fails when the
  declaration and that list disagree.

### Removed

- `list_meetings`, which Granola no longer serves, from the declaration, the known tools, the default rules, the
  `granola` skill and the docs. The skill browses with `search_meetings` and no keywords instead.

- **Exports are bounded.** An export takes 1 to 20 meetings and at most 8 MB; a transcript that does not fit is cut with a note. The file goes outside the project, so OpenCode also asks for `external_directory`.
- **`give_feedback` reaches Granola's team.** It is allowed by default, and the skill tells the model to send it only when the user asks.

## [0.0.0] - 2026-11-10

### Added

- `access`, the plugin option every OpenCode plugin of this family has: `"all"` (the default), `"ask-changes"` and
  `"read-only"`. It generates the default permission block from the tool classes, and `/granola-status` shows it in the
  `Access` row and in the status RPC's `access` field.
- `assets/icon-128.png` and `assets/icon-256.png`, with `opencode.icons` and `opencode.vendor` in `package.json`, and
  `scripts/check-icons.mjs`, the family icon contract's check.

### Changed

- Each Granola skill's first line says how to sign in when the tools are absent: `/connect`, or on Jelly `jelly_connection_request`.

- **Every Granola tool is allowed by default.** The plugin's generated block allows every known tool and the `granola_*`
  namespace, so a tool Granola adds later runs without a prompt too, `give_feedback` is no longer off, and the export is
  no longer an ask. Restrict it with `access`, with an agent's own rules, or with a rule per tool; the README's
  Permissions section and SECURITY say what an all-allow default means here.
- The export folder is outside the project, so OpenCode asks for `external_directory` as well as the export's own
  action. A refusal that names it costs nothing and becomes `EXPORT_PATH_NOT_PERMITTED`, whose next step is that rule.
- `docs/scripting.md` is the family's scripting contract: the strict envelope, the location section and its unload note,
  the result wording, and the refusal table, with an example-parsing test.
- `PLUGIN_CODES` and `RPC_CODES` are the one typed code table, checked against the README, the configuration guide and
  the scripting guide.
- The CI has an `actionlint` job, and `npm run check` runs `actionlint` and the icon check.
- The docs' tested-host sentences are checked against `TESTED_HOSTS`, and the README prints the default block in full.
- tools RPC v2: every known tool is scriptable. Granola's writes, `give_feedback` (a send)
  and the plugin's `export_markdown` (an export, confined to the export folder) are methods now, so a script can write,
  send or export with the session's allow; `sign_out` stays outside, since the plugin removes it. The shared tools RPC
  module is updated in place and `scripts/check-copies.mjs` pins its v2 hash. Every method carries a class, and
  `describe` reports it, plus each method's resolved `permission` when given a session.
- A call resolves the rule before dispatch: only an `allow` runs, an `ask` is refused, and a `deny` is refused, with no
  tool call and no prompt. A saved "Always allow" no longer authorises an ad-hoc script; its grant is a rule in config,
  or a Jobs run session.

### Known limits

- **Granola's server decides what the tools reach.** The plugin registers the tools Granola's server lists. A tool Granola adds later is not classed by the plugin: the `access` option decides whether it runs, asks or is denied, and `/granola-status` counts it as unknown.

- **Exports are bounded.** An export takes 1 to 20 meetings and at most 8 MB; a transcript that does not fit is cut with a note. The file goes outside the project, so OpenCode also asks for `external_directory`.
- **`give_feedback` reaches Granola's team.** It is allowed by default, and the skill tells the model to send it only when the user asks.
- **No retries.** The plugin does not retry a failed call. The error names the next step.
- **Hosts and platforms.** The plugin is tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5 and 2.2.6, and runs on macOS or Linux. A later 2.2 release starts and is reported as untested.
